paragraphs: Friend, here's what this long list teaches me: the family line keeps going. Er is called wicked (1 Chronicles 2:3), Achar brought trouble upon Israel (1 Chronicles 2:7), and Jeconiah is called the captive (1 Chronicles 3:17). Messy names, messy family, and the tree keeps right on growing. I've burned a batch or two myself and kept baking, so I respect a family that won't quit.

Now look at who else gets written down. Seled died without children (1 Chronicles 2:30), and so did Jether (1 Chronicles 2:32), and both names are still in the list. Sheshan had only daughters, and his Egyptian servant Jarha married one of them, and their line runs on for generations (1 Chronicles 2:34-41). Tamar, whose place in Judah's story is complicated, bore Perez and Zerah (1 Chronicles 2:4), and the list says so plainly. Nobody gets skipped for being complicated.

So here's what I want you to carry out of this one, baker. If the list has room for a captive, a servant and a man who died without children, I think there's room for your story too, even the crumbly parts. You don't have to be the tidiest cookie in the box to be counted. Keep your oven ready, friend, because the story isn't over.
